title: Photorespiration (C₂ Cycle) & The Three-Organelle Axis
topic: RuBisCO Oxygenase, 25% Carbon Loss, Chloroplast-Peroxisome-Mitochondria Cascade, & Glycine-Serine Reaction
topics: Photorespiration Definition & RuBisCO Oxygenase Dual Activity
Net Energetic Waste: Consumes ATP and O2, Releases CO2, Produces NO ATP/NADPH (25% Carbon Loss)
Three-Organelle Cooperative Axis: Chloroplast -> Peroxisome -> Mitochondria
Peroxisomal Glycolate Oxidase & Catalase Scavenging of $\text{H}_2\text{O}_2$
Return to Chloroplast: Hydroxypyruvate -> Glycerate -> Phosphorylation to 3-PGA
quickSummary: Photorespiration (C2 cycle) is triggered when RuBisCO acts as an oxygenase under low CO2, high O2, and high temperatures, converting RuBP (5C) + O2 into 3-PGA (3C) and toxic 2-phosphoglycolate (2C). The scavenging cascade spans three organelles: Chloroplast (2-phosphoglycolate -> glycolate) -> Peroxisome (glycolate -> glyoxylate + H2O2 -> glycine) -> Mitochondria (2 Glycine -> 1 Serine + CO2 + NH3) -> Peroxisome (serine -> hydroxypyruvate -> glycerate) -> Chloroplast (glycerate + ATP -> 3-PGA). It results in a 25% net loss of fixed carbon without generating ATP or NADPH.

summaryBox.title: Quick Section Summary
summaryBox.takeaway: RuBisCO oxygenase produces 3-PGA (3C) + 2-phosphoglycolate (2C). Cooperatively operates across Chloroplast -> Peroxisome -> Mitochondria. 25% fixed carbon is lost as CO2.

conceptBreakdown.codeSnippet:
PHOTORESPIRATORY THREE-ORGANELLE AXIS
                        
   CHLOROPLAST                 PEROXISOME                  MITOCHONDRIA
   RuBP + O₂                    Glycolate                  Glycine (2C) + Glycine (2C)
     │                             │                             │
   2-Phosphoglycolate ──► Glycolate ──► Glyoxylate ──► Glycine ──► Serine (3C) + CO₂ + NH₃
     ▲                             ▲                             │
   3-PGA ◄── Glycerate ◄───────────┴── Hydroxypyruvate ◄─────────┘
conceptBreakdown.content:
Under elevated temperatures and high $\text{O}_2:\text{CO}_2$ ratios in $C_3$ plants, RuBisCO functions as an oxygenase:
$$\Large \mathbf{\text{RuBP (5C)} + \text{O}_2 \xrightarrow{\text{RuBisCO Oxygenase}} \text{3-PGA (3C)} + \text{2-Phosphoglycolate (2C)}}$$
• Results in **$25\%$ loss of previously fixed carbon**, consumes $\text{ATP}$ and $\text{O}_2$, releases $\text{CO}_2$, and produces **NO $\text{ATP}$ or $\text{NADPH}$**.

conceptBreakdown.heading: 8.1 Three-Organelle Enzymatic Steps
conceptBreakdown.title: 8.1 Three-Organelle Enzymatic Steps
conceptBreakdown.content:
1. **Chloroplast**: 2-Phosphoglycolate is dephosphorylated by phosphoglycolate phosphatase to form **Glycolate (2C)**, exported across the chloroplast envelope.
2. **Peroxisome**: Glycolate is oxidized by **Glycolate Oxidase** to **Glyoxylate**, producing $\text{H}_2\text{O}_2$ (scavenged by **Catalase**). Glutamate-glyoxylate aminotransferase converts glyoxylate to the amino acid **Glycine (2C)**.
3. **Mitochondria**: Two molecules of Glycine ($2\text{C} + 2\text{C}$) are converted by the **Glycine Decarboxylase Multienzyme Complex** into one molecule of **Serine (3C)**:
   $$\mathbf{2\text{ Glycine (2C)} + \text{NAD}^+ + \text{H}_2\text{O} \longrightarrow 1\text{ Serine (3C)} + 1\text{ CO}_2\uparrow + 1\text{ NH}_3\uparrow + 1\text{ NADH} + \text{H}^+}$$
4. **Return Path**: Serine returns to the Peroxisome $\rightarrow$ converted to Hydroxypyruvate $\rightarrow$ reduced to Glycerate $\rightarrow$ re-enters Chloroplast $\rightarrow$ phosphorylated using **$1\text{ ATP}$** by Glycerate Kinase to yield **3-PGA** (salvaging $75\%$ of carbon).
